refs.quote: The following serious adverse reactions are discussed elsewhere in the labeling: • Hepatic Injury [see Warnings and Precautions (5.1) ] • Serious Skin Reactions [see Warnings and Precautions (5.2) ] • Allergy and Hypersensitivity [see Warnings and Precautions (5.4) ]

In acute acetaminophen overdosage, dose-dependent, potentially fatal hepatic necrosis is the most serious adverse effect. Renal tubular necrosis, hypoglycemic coma, and thrombocytopenia may also occur.

mechanism_of_action.value: The precise mechanism of the analgesic and antipyretic properties of acetaminophen is not established but is thought to primarily involve central actions.

refs.quote: The precise mechanism of the analgesic and antipyretic properties of acetaminophen is not established but is thought to primarily involve central actions.

Acetaminophen is primarily metabolized in the liver by first-order kinetics and involves three principal separate pathways: Conjugation with glucuronide, conjugation with sulfate, and oxidation via the cytochrome P450 enzyme pathway, primarily CYP2E1, to form a reactive intermediate metabolite (N-acetyl-p-benzoquinone imine or NAPQI).

enzyme_profile.note: Metabolized via glucuronidation, sulfation, and CYP2E1 oxidation to NAPQI.

value.effect: Substances that induce or regulate CYP2E1 may alter acetaminophen metabolism and increase its hepatotoxic potential; excessive ethanol can induce hepatic cytochromes while also acting as a competitive inhibitor.
value.management: Monitor for hepatotoxicity; clinical consequences of CYP2E1 induction have not been established.

refs.locator: 7.1 Effects of Other Substances on Acetaminophen
refs.quote: Substances that induce or regulate hepatic cytochrome enzyme CYP2E1 may alter the metabolism of acetaminophen and increase its hepatotoxic potential. The clinical consequences of these effects have not been established.

value.effect: Chronic oral acetaminophen use at 4000 mg/day has been shown to increase INR in some patients stabilized on sodium warfarin.
value.management: More frequent assessment of INR may be appropriate when administering acetaminophen in patients on oral anticoagulants.

refs.quote: Chronic oral acetaminophen use at a dose of 4000 mg/day has been shown to cause an increase in international normalized ratio (INR) in some patients who have been stabilized on sodium warfarin as an anticoagulant.

As no studies have been performed evaluating the short-term use of acetaminophen injection in patients on oral anticoagulants, more frequent assessment of INR may be appropriate in such circumstances.

tier.note: Large human epidemiological cohorts (n=26,424 prospective; n=11,610 case-control) with oral acetaminophen showed no increased risk of major birth defects, but methodological limitations prevent definitely ruling out risk, no animal reproduction studies exist for IV acetaminophen, and published oral animal studies at 0.85-1.2x MHDD showed fetotoxicity, fetal liver/kidney necrosis, and reduced fertility.

refs.quote: Published epidemiological studies with oral acetaminophen use during pregnancy have not reported a clear association with acetaminophen use and birth defects, miscarriage, or adverse maternal or fetal outcomes [see Data] . Animal reproduction studies have not been conducted with IV acetaminophen.
However, these studies cannot definitely establish the absence of any risk because of methodological limitations, including recall bias.

lactation_rid.value: 1% to 2% of the weight-adjusted maternal dose

refs.quote: Average and maximum neonatal doses of 1% and 2%, respectively, of the weight-adjusted maternal dose are reported after a single oral administration of 1 gram APAP.

lactation_summary.value: Passes rapidly into human milk with similar milk and plasma levels (1% average, 2% maximum weight-adjusted maternal dose after 1 g oral); one documented case of rash in a breastfed infant that resolved upon discontinuation and recurred on rechallenge.

refs.quote: However, limited published studies report that acetaminophen passes rapidly into human milk with similar levels in the milk and plasma.
There is one well-documented report of a rash in a breast-fed infant that resolved when the mother stopped acetaminophen use and recurred when she resumed acetaminophen use.
